children.text: Precession of the Earth's axis

Investigate the historical problem's Newtonian model of axial precession. Earth is a homogeneous oblate spheroid with equatorial radius Re, polar radius Rp, mean R=(Re+Rp)/2 and small flattening hmax=Re−Rp. Take G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) N m²/kg², R=\(6.371\times10^{6}\) m, ME=\(5.972\times10^{24}\) kg, Sun mass MS=\(1.989\times10^{30}\) kg at distance dSE=\(1.496\times10^{11}\) m, Moon mass MM=\(7.348\times10^{22}\) kg at dME=\(3.844\times10^{8}\) m, and tilt α=23.5°. Use one rotation in 24 hours and one year of 365.25 days. After part A use the empirical hmax=21 km irrespective of your estimate. For solar averaging replace the Sun by a uniform circular ring in the ecliptic plane. Set z perpendicular to that plane, with origin at Earth's centre. Near Earth all distances r,|z| are much smaller than the ring radius.

statement.text:

Investigate the historical problem's Newtonian model of axial precession. Earth is a homogeneous oblate spheroid with equatorial radius Re, polar radius Rp, mean R=(Re+Rp)/2 and small flattening hmax=Re−Rp. Take G=\(6.67\times10^{-11}\) N m²/kg², R=\(6.371\times10^{6}\) m, ME=\(5.972\times10^{24}\) kg, Sun mass MS=\(1.989\times10^{30}\) kg at distance dSE=\(1.496\times10^{11}\) m, Moon mass MM=\(7.348\times10^{22}\) kg at dME=\(3.844\times10^{8}\) m, and tilt α=23.5°. In \(h_{max}\propto G^{-1}\omega^\beta M_E^\gamma R^\delta\), find β,γ,δ.

Assume the dimensionless factor is one and evaluate hmax.
b.1. Ring field on its axis

b.2. Ring field in its plane

d.2. Solar-only numerical period
Evaluate T1 in years using hmax=21 km.
e.1. Lunar correction factor

e.2. Combined numerical period

children.text: Precession of the Earth's axis
a.1. Flattening dimensions
Using [G]=L³M^−1T^−2, dimensional balance gives time exponent 2−β=0, mass exponent 1+γ=0 and length exponent δ−3=1. Thus β=2, γ=−1, δ=4.
a.2. Flattening estimate
\(\omega=2\pi/86400=7.27\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Therefore \(h_{max}=\omega^2R^4/(GM_E)\simeq21.9\,\mathrm{km}\).
b.1. Ring field on its axis
The exact potential is \(\Phi(z)=-GM_S/\sqrt{d_{SE}^2+z^2}\). Thus \(g_z=-GM_Sz/(d_{SE}^2+z^2)^{3/2}\simeq-GM_Sz/d_{SE}^3\). It points toward the ecliptic plane for either sign of z.
b.2. Ring field in its plane

Symmetry and the mass-free divergence condition near the centre give \(2g_r/r+\partial_zg_z=0\), so \[g_r=GM_Sr/(2d_{SE}^3),\] radially outwards. Alternatively expand the ring potential through r²: \(\Phi(r)=-GM_S/d_{SE}-GM_Sr^2/(4d_{SE}^3)\), then differentiate. The axial restoring field and in-plane outward field have opposite signs.
c.1. Mass of one removed cap
The spheroid volume is \(4\pi R_e^2R_p/3\). Half the difference from a sphere is \(2\pi R_e^2h_{max}/3\). Multiply by density \(3M_E/(4\pi R_e^2R_p)\) to obtain \(m=M_Eh_{max}/(2R_p)\).
c.2. Solar torque

A complete sphere has zero torque, so Earth's torque is opposite that on the removed masses. Both the vertical restoring and radial outward fields contribute. Their combined torque magnitude is \(6GmM_SR^2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha/(5d_{SE}^3)\). Substitute m≈MEhmax/(2R): \[|\tau|=\frac{3GM_EM_SR h_{max}}{5d_{SE}^3}\sin\alpha\cos\alpha.\] If the north axis lies in +xz, this torque is along −y, giving retrograde precession.
d.1. Solar-only precession period

To leading order the spin angular momentum is \(L=(2/5)M_ER^2\omega\). The magnitude changes slowly compared with direction. Precession gives \(|\dot{\mathbf L}|=\Omega_1L\sin\alpha=|\tau|\). Hence \[T_1=\frac{2\pi}{\Omega_1}=\frac{4\pi d_{SE}^3R\omega}{3GM_Sh_{max}\cos\alpha}.\]
d.2. Solar-only numerical period
The model gives \(T_1\simeq8.06\times10^4\) years. This is larger than the observed precession period because the Moon has not yet been included.
e.1. Lunar correction factor

The same ring calculation applies and torque coefficients add as M/d³. Thus \[\frac{T_2}{T_1}=\frac{M_S/d_{SE}^3}{M_S/d_{SE}^3+M_M/d_{ME}^3}.\] The lunar torque makes precession faster and the period shorter.
e.2. Combined numerical period
The ratio is approximately 0.315. Multiplying the solar-only period gives \(T_2\simeq2.54\times10^4\) years in this homogeneous-Earth, coplanar-circular-orbit model.
